artboards.title: Module page — Piston Honda MK III

annotations.text:
eurorack.fi — 29 items, 16 eurorack (207 HP) + 13 standalone. Two collections: spongefile 9, Sampo 20.

Finnish blue only — the palette switcher is gone. Theme follows the OS unless you pick one.

Specs, HP, categories and outbound ModularGrid links are real. Sampo's wish list is the last placeholder on the site.

BOTH collections trade. The card signal is WHOSE it is — the name, with a dot for recall. Colour cannot carry ten sellers.

Wish content lives on its own page now, not inline on Home. Home's wish band is a short text-chip teaser; clicking it goes to Toiveet — see that artboard — which shows the full recognition grid per seller. Clicking a seller's grid on Toiveet is meant to return to Home with the owner filter pre-set to that seller.

There is no sold state: items no longer for sale are deleted outright.

Two phone frames at 390. The module page is the SAME file as the 1280 one — one responsive source, two frames.

Inherited breakpoints from index.html: 900 / 720 / 640.

NOTE: the site does not offer try-before-you-buy. Trust comes from being a named local collective, not from testing. Do not reintroduce come-and-hear-it copy.

Three languages, opens in Finnish. Finnish is written AS Finnish — "Other stuff" is "Muut".

Per-listing prose is English-only for now, so the missing-translation banner is the NORMAL state on module pages, not an edge case.

Nav is three items: Everything / What we want / Contact. "Why not tori" was cut.
Designed — see the Admin & brand page.

Add a listing. Type maker + model, everything else is fetched and stays editable.

Every value carries its source: solid blue = ModularGrid, dashed amber = generated. The price shows the listings behind it, never a bare number.

Finnish and Swedish are both required — Publish is disabled while Swedish is missing, and machine translation is offered but flagged for a read-through, never applied silently.

Delta-V specs are real. The used-price comparisons are placeholders.

The o is a 3.5 mm jack — nut ring and plug.

Spacing was measured, not eyeballed: the word set with a real o puts 4px either side of it at 86px. The ring needs a little more air than a solid bowl, so it sits at 6px / 6px — even, and still one word.

Only the full stop before fi takes the accent. The favicon is a simplified derivative, not a constraint on the mark.

A: original vs current, with the numbers.
B: seven variants on the jack.
C: a different approach — the name as a faceplate between rails, no letter substitution.

Judged on how each reads at real sizes, not on surviving 16px.

Dedicated wish-list page — nav item 2's real destination.

Flow: Home's wish band (text chips) is a teaser — click it, land here. Here, each seller's whole card is a link back to Home with the owner filter pre-applied to them.

Neither hop is a real navigation in this mockup — every .dc.html is its own sandboxed artboard, there is no cross-artboard router here. Both links are drawn as the real, working thing they need to become; dev builds the actual routing/filter-param behaviour.

spongefile's five wants are real, drawn to true HP scale. Sampo's four are still placeholder — dashed outline, no panel, on purpose.
